description:
Hi! I’m a student interested in creativity, technology, and game development. My project focuses on creating a fun and engaging game.

I’m looking for teammates who are creative, responsible, and willing to share ideas. Skills in programming, game design, graphic design, storytelling, and sound design would be helpful.

You don’t need to be an expert. Beginners are welcome as long as you’re willing to learn, contribute, and work together as a team. Let’s turn our ideas into reality!
summary:
What we develop
- An interactive, first-person aerospace command simulation set on Mars during a severe blackout and dust storm.
- Players manage critical life-support systems, monitor battery power, inspect vent cameras for smoke, and use a dust monitor to seal breaches.
- Features tactile control interfaces, wiring mini-games for equipment repairs, and optional live data integration from NASA APIs.

How it does address the challenge
- Translates complex space exploration data, rover weather reports, and astronaut survival protocols into an engaging, educational gaming experience.
- Educates users on real-world challenges faced by space missions, such as solar particle events, dust storms, energy management, and equipment maintenance.

Why it is important
- Inspires interest in space science and aerospace engineering among students and the public through gamified learning.
- Promotes critical thinking, resource management, and problem-solving skills under simulated emergency conditions.
details:
• What it does and how it works
    • It is an interactive, first-person command simulation where players act as a base commander on Mars during a severe dust storm blackout.
    • Players must balance system resources (power, oxygen, and health) over a five-day survival period.
    • It works by combining real-time telemetry tracking, a camera observation system to spot smoke and leaks, a dust checker to detect hazardous air, and interactive mini-games (such as wiring puzzles) to repair malfunctioning equipment.
    • Provides an immersive, educational experience that teaches players about space exploration challenges, resource management, and problem-solving under pressure.
    • Offers adjustable gameplay modes, including normal and hard difficulties, plus an optional Live Mission mode that syncs with real NASA solar and Mars weather data.
    • Inspires interest in space science, astronomy, and STEM fields by transforming complex space data into a gamified, accessible format.
    • Encourages critical thinking and strategic planning as players learn how real-world space missions handle emergencies and environmental hazards.
    • Built using web technologies including HTML, CSS, and modern JavaScript, leveraging the Web Audio API for mechanical sound effects and SVG graphics for interactive UI elements and mini-games.
    • Integrates external NASA data feeds (such as DONKI space-weather data and Curiosity rover REMS weather reports) when running in Live Mission mode.
    • Combines classic atmospheric command-room mechanics with modern web development, creating a fully self-contained simulation with rich retro-futuristic visuals (CRT filters, CCTV overlays, and tactile switchboards) directly in the browser.
    • Blends fictional survival storytelling with real-world NASA science data, bridging the gap between gaming and authentic space research.
    • Ensured accessibility and responsive design so the game runs smoothly on both desktop monitors and touch-based mobile devices with custom touch targets and portraits layouts.
    • Balanced gameplay mechanics such as power consumption, oxygen depletion, and equipment failure rates to create a fair yet challenging survival experience.
